landmarks.name: Weldon Library
facts: It is the main library for the arts, humanities and social sciences.

landmarks.name: Thompson Arena
facts: It has an NHL-sized ice rink with an indoor track around it.
It was built in 1971.

landmarks.name: Richard Ivey Building
facts: It is the business school's home.
The business school moved into it from its old building across campus in September 2013.

landmarks.name: Althouse
facts: It is the education faculty's building.
Its most unusual feature is a circular library added in 1966, nicknamed the flying saucer.

landmarks.name: Elborn College
facts: The library and information science program was housed here from 1982 to 1998.

landmarks.name: Western Student Recreation Centre
facts: It is the main gym for fitness classes, intramural sports and clubs.
It opened in January 2009.

landmarks.name: FIMS & Nursing Building
facts: It is shared by the media studies faculty and a health sciences program, at Lambton Drive and Huron Drive.
It was built in 2016.

landmarks.name: Brescia University College
facts: It was Canada's last women's university college.
It was affiliated with Western from 1919 until 2024.

landmarks.name: Thames Hall
facts: Before the recreation centre opened in 2009, it housed the athletics department, with a pool and a gym.

landmarks.name: North Campus Building
facts: The information and media studies faculty was based here from 2006 to 2017.

landmarks.name: Talbot College
facts: The music library has been on its second floor since 1972.
It was renovated and expanded together with the Music Building, finishing in 2018.

landmarks.name: Amit Chakma Engineering Building
facts: It is the newest engineering building, named after a former university president.
Its name was announced on October 12, 2018.

landmarks.name: University College
facts: It is one of the two oldest academic buildings on the central campus, with its Gothic tower.
It was built as the Arts Building and completed in 1924, designed by John Moore and Co.

landmarks.name: Natural Sciences Building
facts: A science reading room opened in it in 1947 because the main library was out of space.

landmarks.name: Alumni Hall
facts: It is used for convocation, basketball, volleyball and other indoor events.
It was built as a multi-purpose hall in the late 1960s.

landmarks.name: Music Building
facts: It was renovated and expanded together with Talbot College, finishing in 2018.

landmarks.name: Middlesex College
facts: Its clock tower is a campus landmark, and the computer science department is based here.
The library and information science program was housed here from 1998 to 2004.

landmarks.name: Lawson Hall
facts: It houses the History, English and Writing Studies, Classical Studies and Women's Studies departments.

landmarks.name: Western Interdisciplinary Research Building
facts: Students call it WIRB; it houses the Brain and Mind Institute.
